BENCH = ITER2/gen_art_experiment_11/bench/<task>/ (spec.json, tests.jsonl, checker.py, references/, ast_rules.py, runtime_rules.py, probes.json, gold_set.jsonl, forced_programs.jsonl; verify sha256 against bench/commitment.json). Path tasks T1 grid and T2 weighted shortest path: ITER2/gen_art_experiment_8/suite and engine.py. Twin nouns: ITER2/gen_art_experiment_7/frozen/templates_nouns_padding.json. Known solutions for novelty audits: ITER3/gen_art_experiment_18/results/known_solutions_summary.json. MODELS: Qwen/Qwen3-8B (revision b968826d) and Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base (revision 49e3418f), thinking off (enable_thinking=False) unless an arm says otherwise; the base model receives the IDENTICAL chat-templated token ids; never hold two 8B models on the GPU at once (states a hook needs from another model are computed in a separate pass and cached to disk). HARDWARE: the planned pod is an RTX A4500 (Ampere, compute capability 8.6, 20 GB, no FP8 tensor cores, 29 GB RAM). Default engine W16A16 = bf16 HF transformers with a memory-probed batch (expect 4-8 at <= 1,536 tokens). vLLM bf16 is allowed only for UNHOOKED sampling (twin top-ups beyond the first 50 CRN slots, base samples, forced programs), with an engine-equivalence check: label-composition Jensen-Shannon divergence between >= 50 HF and >= 50 vLLM draws of the same cell against a template-resampling null. Every row logs precision (W8A8 / W8A16 / W16A8 / W16A16), checkpoint, kernel and the sha256 of the hook code; no comparison crosses precisions except inside the engine-control artifact. HOOK CODE (reuse, never rewrite): exp17/exp19 make_edits RAND, displacement-targeted: delta = h - h_twin_clean, h <- h + (alpha * n[l,p] - delta . u) u at every task-specification position of the hooked blocks during prefill only; exp20 site hooks for other sites. DOSE: the ban-free unit n[l,p] = ||h_twin[l,p]|| x r_Q(l) unless an arm says otherwise; every push logs per position the realised displacement norm, its ratio to the residual norm, the ban-free unit and, on the 15 existing tasks, the iteration-4 ban unit; dose summaries are reported both as the mean of per-position ratios and as the ratio of mean norms. DECODING: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, no top-k, max_new_tokens 1,024 (path tasks 1,536); one uniform stream per (unit, template, slot) shared by every arm of the artifact, so per-sample flips are exact. TEMPLATES: the frozen twin templates W1-W5 with the unit's neutral noun padded with ' .'; N per cell = 5 templates x N/5. No ban prompt is rendered for any new unit (grep audit of every rendered prompt before each commitment). DEFAULT: the twin's modal correct label at N >= 50 (N 300 where L is scored) with share >= 0.6, else NO DEFAULT (the unit enters no landing or movability test). LABELS: frozen gated labellers (runtime tracer primary, AST second, blind OpenRouter judge on disagreement only); a style re-gate per family and per new unit; base outputs audited with a 15-program blind sample per unit by two judge families; 'other' and 'invalid' are separate columns and 'other' never counts as a landing. CORRECT := passes the hidden tests within the per-case limits. L INSTRUMENTS (frozen definitions, identical in every artifact): q_tail = add-one-smoothed composition, over the non-default catalogue algorithms plus 'other', of the correct non-default programs among 300 twin samples (200 at T 1.0 and 100 at T 1.3, same CRN slot ids); t_u = its most frequent correct non-default algorithm; TAIL-EMPTY = no correct non-default program in the 300. q_lik = for each non-default catalogue algorithm, the mean over 10 name-scrubbed, test-passing forced programs of the teacher-forced log-probability, under the twin prompt (averaged over W1-W5), of the first 48 code tokens; its top-1 is the argmax; for log scores a softmax of the per-token-normalised scores (raw version beside). q_base = add-one-smoothed correct-only composition of Qwen3-8B-Base over >= 200 chat-template samples plus 100 plain completions (below 20 correct programs: attempts, flagged); r_u = its most frequent non-default algorithm; per unit the valid and correct support counts are reported. LANDING EVENT = a (unit, nudge type) pair with >= 5 correct off-default programs pooled over that nudge type's cells whose pass rate is >= 0.8 x the twin's; the modal landing must lead the next algorithm by 15 points, else 'no clear landing' (a miss for every forecast in top-1, scored normally in log score). DISCORDANT = r_u differs from q_lik's top-1. MATCHED EVENTS: every forecast comparison uses the same events; an undefined forecast is scored as uniform and the defined-only result is reported beside it. PSEUDO-REPLICATION GUARD: beside every per-event test, a unit-clustered version (one pooled landing per unit over its content-free nudge types; cluster permutation p); if only the per-event version passes, the claim is written 'per event, not per unit'. M CANDIDATES (frozen definitions): beta = q_base's correct-only share off the instruct default; REPLACEMENT CLASS = the base model's modal correct algorithm differs from the instruct default; RUNTIME MERIT = log2(median runtime of the default reference / median runtime of the fastest correct non-default reference) over the hidden stress cases, one harness, 5 repeats; TWIN MODAL SHARE at N 300; K = catalogue size; FORK MARGIN m = the twin's teacher-forced log-probability of the default's forced openings minus that of r_u's openings (first 48 code tokens, same passes as q_lik). ESCAPE: 8 fresh fixed isotropic directions (seeds disjoint from every earlier directions/ folder) at the task-specification positions of blocks 12-23; a cell passes at N 10 if its correct off-default share is >= twin + 0.20 with pass >= 0.8 x twin, then gets 20 more slots and is a CONFIRMED escape only if the pooled 30 keep the excess with one-sided exact binomial p < 0.05 against the twin's off-default rate; E_u(alpha) = confirmed escapes / 8; E_u = mean over the alphas run. METRICS: correct-only rarefied Hill-1 at depth 25 (flag below 25 correct), off-default share, correct compositions beside attempted ones; every maximum over directions reported beside its distribution. PRICES (where used): H5, P15 and P20 on the full-simplex randomisation hull, edge-restricted hull as a sensitivity, 2,000 bootstrap replicates with the maximum over settings inside each replicate. COMMITMENTS: before the first decisive sample of each unit or arm, write predictions, thresholds, analysis code and input hashes to predictions/ and append sha256 + UTC to commitments.log as a hash chain; never edit a committed file. SCALING: every arm runs 10 -> 100 -> full with time per sample logged and extrapolated before the full run; N drops (never below 30 on a decisive cell) before any arm drops, then the artifact's drop order applies; drops are decided on time only, never on outcomes. NOVELTY AUDIT: every CORRECT program labelled 'other' is read by two blind judges from different model families (cheap OpenRouter models), a third resolves disagreements, and a blind manual comparison with the nearest known solutions follows; classes NOVEL ALGORITHM / CATALOGUE VARIANT (named) / KNOWN TECHNIQUE OUTSIDE THE CATALOGUE / LABELLER MISS / DEGENERATE; 'no correct novel algorithm' only at a count of 0, with the rule-of-three bound. OPENROUTER: judge calls only, base_url=os.environ['OPENROUTER_BASE_URL'], api_key=os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY'], cheapest adequate models, a running total from usage.cost, the artifact's cap, and stop the whole batch at the first HTTP 403 whose message starts 'AI Inventor per-run OpenRouter budget'. OUTPUT: per-sample JSONL rows {model, unit, unit_kind, arm, site, precision, lambda, alpha, direction_seed, template, slot, temperature, thinking, prompt_sha256, label, labeller_source, passed, finish_reason, n_new_tokens, realised_disp, code_sha256, code}; method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out) with every analysis in metadata; figures/ (PDF + PNG); README.md with a 'Restoring removed files' section; .aii/manifest.yaml (cached states and activation tensors: keep, on the run volume, never published).
strings.PANEL: PANEL PROTOCOL v6 (identical in both panel artifacts; they differ only in their candidate lists and their extra arm). WHY TWO PANELS: building gated units is the bottleneck, and L1's power is the number of decisive events (tail-empty and discordant); two parallel panels with disjoint pre-registered lists and one frozen protocol make 16-20 new gated units likely. BUILD AND GATE (per candidate, in list order; reuse exp26's unit builder, sandbox tracer, CRN engine and judges): (1) a frozen specification in new wording (I/O format, constraints, >= 50 tokens, no algorithm or data-structure word) from the LeetCode or KodCode rows of art_j3Rm_lr2nzR6 (full_data_out.json: leetcodedataset rows carry I/O pairs, kodcode_algorithmic rows test-verified solutions); (2) hidden tests: the source cases plus seeded generated and stress cases, per-case limits max(1 s, 10 x the fastest reference), an order-free checker where answers are not unique; (3) a catalogue of >= 3 mechanistically distinct algorithms (different asymptotics, data structures or invariants; recursion versus iteration is phrasing; a library call is its own mode), each with a reference passing every hidden test at <= 0.25 x the limit, and mutants that fail; (4) runtime-signature and AST rules with probes, modelled on the bench's runtime_rules.py and ast_rules.py; (5) a gold set (every reference, 10 base-pilot and 10 instruct programs, two blind judges from different families, a third on disagreement). GATE: references 100%, runtime-versus-AST Cohen's kappa >= 0.8, runtime versus adjudicated >= 0.9, one revision round; a failing unit is excluded and listed with its numbers and is never replaced by a disguised variant; exclusions decided before the build (fewer than 3 distinct correct algorithms) are logged with the reason. Mid-artifact rule: if fewer than 5 units have gated at half the artifact's time, the reserves are built in order and the shortfall is reported. ENROLMENT ORDER (predictors only; fixed here): as each unit gates, compute its base pilot (Qwen3-8B-Base, chat template, N 30, the first 30 of its 200), its forced programs and q_lik, and its first 50 twin samples (CRN). Units whose pilot runner-up differs from q_lik's top-1, or whose twin has no correct non-default program at N 50, enter the nudge protocol first (they are where L1a and L1b can be decided); every other gated unit follows while time remains; the order and its inputs are hashed before any nudge, and the analysis reports the all-enrolled result beside. This selects on the predictors, never on an outcome. PER UNIT, IN THIS ORDER: (a) forced programs: bench-style 'Implement X' forced prompts until 10 name-scrubbed, test-passing programs per catalogue algorithm (flag algorithms below 10 after 40 attempts); (b) q_lik; (c) the twin of 300 (the first 50 on the HF CRN engine; the remaining 150 at T 1.0 and 100 at T 1.3 may use unhooked vLLM bf16 under the engine-equivalence check) -> default or NO DEFAULT, q_tail, t_u, TAIL-EMPTY; (d) the base repertoire: 200 chat-template + 100 plain-completion samples -> q_base, r_u, valid and correct support counts, the 15-program audit by two judge families; (e) the M candidates; (f) COMMIT by sha256, before the unit's first nudge: q_base, q_lik, q_tail, r_u, t_u, the discordance and tail-empty flags, support counts, M values, and the predicted landing (= r_u); (g) NUDGES: the escape population (8 fresh fixed directions x alpha 1, 2 and 4 x N 10, confirmed at N 30); per-sample plan noise PN (a fresh isotropic direction per sample, blocks 12-23, prefill only) at alpha 2 and 4 (N 50 each); generated-token noise GTN at alpha 2 (exp20's S3 hook on generated tokens 1-32, N 50); base intent BINT (exp27's code: Qwen3-8B-Base writes the one-sentence intent, Qwen3-8B writes the code; N 30; not content-free, so it enters K and is reported beside the landings, never in L1). ANALYSIS (each panel reports its own half; both write landing_events.json and units.json in schema iter6_landing_v1 (one row per landing event: unit, nudge type, cells pooled, correct off-default counts per algorithm, modal landing and margin, default, K, r_u, q_lik top-1, t_u, TAIL-EMPTY and DISCORDANT flags, q_base, q_lik and q_tail vectors, support counts, commit hash), and both implement pool_l1.py from the frozen specification in this protocol and commit it before their first nudge; the next round's Step 0 runs both implementations on the pooled files, and they must agree): L1a = on TAIL-EMPTY events, the base runner-up equals the modal landing in >= 2/3 of events, exact Poisson-binomial p < 0.05 against per-event chance 1/(K-1), on >= 6 events (fewer: descriptive, carried to iteration 7); L1b = on DISCORDANT events, the base runner-up versus q_lik's top-1 as the forecast of the modal landing, one-sided exact sign test p < 0.05 on >= 6 events; supporting log scores of q_base against q_lik and against q_tail on matched events (non-inferiority: one-sided 95% bootstrap bound on the mean difference above -0.10 nats); the rival t_u (the twin's most frequent non-default program) scored top-1 where defined; the unit-clustered version beside every test. L2 = no correct nudged program lands on an algorithm with zero valid and zero correct base programs (rule-of-three bound). L3 = among non-default algorithms, the split-half held-out log score of q_base raised to a fitted power against uniform-over-survivors, association (20 'standard alternative to <default>' answers from the instruct model, mapped with the catalogue lexicon) and q_tail; pooled Kendall tau between the base and tail orders with a sign test. M = Spearman of each frozen candidate with E_u over the new units (one-sided, Holm across candidates, supported at >= 0.5), with the screen ranking from Step 0 beside it. K = H5, P15 and P20 of BINT, PN alpha 2 and 4 on the full-simplex hull per new unit. DISCONFIRMING (named in advance): q_lik or q_tail does at least as well as the base and the base runner-up is at chance on tail-empty events: nudges walk the tuned model's own hidden ladder, and the base model is a proxy only where tuning kept the order.
